non_blocking_notes: Edge gating is vacuous by construction: the graph has exactly one node, m7-s1, with depends_on []. There is no edge to refute and no cycle. `python3 -c` over steps.json confirms a single id m7-s1, repo RivRetrieve, no gaps, no duplicates, no reference outside m7, no version bump or tag scheduled. The milestone-level edge m7 -> m2 recorded in milestones.json is already satisfied on main (m2 landed at 1b903fa), so its absence inside this graph is correct, not a missing edge.

Quantitative claims verified independently, not taken from the graph. Reading the packaged artifact at the ref with polars over `git show 1b903fa:src/rivretrieve/_internal/providers/ch_foen/catalogue/stations.parquet`: 246 rows, 246 unique station_id, columns (provider_id, station_id, latitude, longitude, crs), and crs unique values == ['unknown']. station_products.parquet is 738 rows with availability unique == ['unknown'] (never 'unavailable'), so the m2 edge rule `availability != 'unavailable'` retains all 738; reproducing _materialize's inner joins against stations and products yields exactly 738 edge rows over 246 unique (provider_id, station_id) pairs. Both the 738 series figure and the 246 unique-marker figure are exact, and the (provider_id, station_id) collapse ratio is genuinely 3:1, so a step that forgot to dedupe would visibly render 738.

Feasibility of the folium claims verified part by part. `git show 1b903fa:tests/test_map_stations.py` defines FakeMap/FakeMarker/FakeFolium at module level and five tests already drive the whole path through `monkeypatch.setattr('rivretrieve._internal.station_map._load_folium', lambda: FakeFolium)`, asserting marker count (246 for providers='ch_foen'), exact popup HTML, and marker location. `git show 1b903fa:tests/test_map_stations.py | sed -n '175,195p'` puts `pytest.importorskip('folium')` on lines 179 and 190 exactly as the step states, and `_load_folium` in station_map.py catches ModuleNotFoundError from `import_module('folium')` and raises MissingOptionalDependencyError. Marker count, popup text, non-narrowing and catalogue immutability are therefore observable offline with no install and no network.

Marker colour is the one acceptance item the fake cannot observe *as currently written*: FakeMarker.__init__ takes only location/tooltip/popup and FakeFolium exposes no Icon, whereas folium colours a marker via `icon=folium.Icon(color=...)`. This is not blocking because tests/test_map_stations.py is inside this step's own work and extending the double (add FakeIcon, accept an icon kwarg) is ordinary implementation freedom, not a new dependency. Flagging it so the executor does not read 'use the existing fake Folium backend' as a prohibition on extending it.

The colour-distinction evidence is materially available offline: reading every packaged stations.parquet at the ref shows crs is 'unknown' for ba_fhmzbih, br_ana, ch_foen, cz_chmi, jp_mlit, no_nve, pl_imgw, th_thaiwater and za_dws, and established for ca_eccc / fr_hubeau / lt_lhmt (EPSG:4326) and usgs_nwis (EPSG:4269). An established-frame selection therefore exists in the wheel without network.

Catalogue immutability is testable and would catch a write-back. discovery.stations() rebuilds from CatalogueReader(record.artifact, ...).read_stations() per registered record, and _as_frame builds a fresh polars frame from the frozen _Series tuples, so a step that wrote EPSG:4326 back onto the artifact or into as_frame output would surface in both read-backs the step names. _Selection, _Series and _EmptyReason are all frozen slots dataclasses, so mutating the selection itself is not even reachable without replacing the object.

Non-narrowing is checkable against real symbols: today the narrowing lives entirely in station_map._filter_stations(providers=, bbox=) called from discovery.map_stations, and the step schedules no bbox/provider parameter on map. Vision Scope-Out bars 'click-to-select mapping, or any capability that narrows a selection'; the step is consistent with that and adds nothing else from Scope-Out.

Retention of the legacy path is respected: map_stations, StationMap and _filter_stations all survive, and tests/test_package.py's deferred-names test still asserts StationMap is absent from the public surface, which the step does not disturb. The existing tests most exposed to the adaptation are test_map_stations_fake_backend_receives_filtered_station_frame (asserts the exact legacy popup string, which has no crs line) and test_station_map_real_backend_renders_five_column_station_frame (line 189, skipped without folium). If the executor adds crs to the shared _station_popup rather than to a selection-specific popup, that first test's literal must be updated in the same commit or the test gate goes red; both routes are merge-green and the choice is the executor's.

'Export only the new map name' is coherent with the exact-name assertion. tests/test_package.py compares module_defined_names to a full set literal, so the assertion must be rewritten to the full 16-name set. The step says exactly that: include this milestone's map name 'while preserving all public names present when the step executes; do not add or remove names owned by another milestone', which is the correct formulation given m9 still owns the legacy deletions.

No lint hazard from the name `map`: ruff select is E,F,W,N,I,UP,B,C4,SIM plus TID251, with flake8-builtins (A) not enabled, and `git show 1b903fa:src/rivretrieve/_internal/discovery.py | grep -n '\bmap('` returns nothing, so shadowing the builtin in discovery.py breaks no existing call site. version_policy NONE is honoured — the graph schedules no bump and no tag.

Minor cosmetic: the step title 'Render selections with explicit coordinate-frame status' differs from milestones.json's m7 title 'Render every selected station with visible CRS status'. Same scope, no behavioural consequence.
summary: Single-node graph, so the edge obligation resolves by inspection: no edges to refute, no cycle, ids clean, and the only milestone-level dependency (m7 -> m2) is already merged at 1b903fa, so omitting it inside the graph is correct rather than a missing edge. The high-risk claims all survive source. I measured the packaged ch_foen artifact myself: 246 station rows, 246 unique station_id, crs uniformly 'unknown', 738 station_products rows none of which are 'unavailable', reproducing to exactly 738 selection series over 246 unique (provider_id, station_id) pairs — both figures in the step are exact, and the 3:1 collapse makes a missing dedupe visible. The fake Folium backend exists and already drives marker count and exact popup text offline; pytest.importorskip('folium') sits on lines 179 and 190 exactly as claimed; _load_folium raises MissingOptionalDependencyError on ModuleNotFoundError. No install and no network are needed, and established-CRS selections (ca_eccc, fr_hubeau, lt_lhmt, usgs_nwis) exist in the wheel for the colour-distinction evidence. Immutability is observable through stations() and _as_frame, both of which rebuild from the artifact and from frozen dataclasses, so a write-back of EPSG:4326 would be caught. map_stations, StationMap and _filter_stations are retained for m9, and the exact-public-name assertion is correctly described as a full-set update. The one gap worth naming is that FakeMarker takes no icon kwarg today, so the colour assertion requires extending the double the step itself owns — implementation freedom, not an unachievable acceptance. APPROVE.
